To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the topological stability of Fermi surfaces and the topological stability in topological insulators/superconductors are rigorously established, and based on this, four topologically distinct kinds of Majorana fermions are revealed in fermionic systems, opening a wider experimental door for searching Majorana fermions.
the boundary-bulk correspondence is a powerful tool to search for new topological types of MFs from topological insulators/superconductors, and the four new types of MFs are discovered.
we have established the general and quantitative relation of the boundary-bulk correspondence between the topological stabilities (stabilities of FSs) of TIs/TSCs and TSCs/TIs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the boundary-bulk correspondence between the topologically stable FSs in fermionic models and the topologically stable gapless edge modes in the corresponding TIs/TSCs, and it is expected to provide a general guideline to search for MFs in the laboratory.
the fundamental problem of how to classify topological types of MFs from boundary-bulk correspondence of TIs/TSCs, which may provide a guideline for searching MFs in experiments.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the existence of a new type of MFs in a one-dimensional superconductor is not a sufficient condition for the existence of a non-trivial topological insulator.
MFs in one dimension are topologically stable and robust against weak disorder, which is a key to search for MFs experimentally.
the boundary-bulk correspondence of topological insulators/superconductors (TIs/TSCs) can be applied to classify the topological stabilities and types of MFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the topological stabilities and types of Fermi surfaces in fermionic systems are closely related to the topological stables and types of TIs/TSCs, and vice versa.

we establish a new topological classification of gapless edge-moded in fermionic systems with PHS, which may be useful for searching new types of MFs experimentally and also for studying topological properties of other systems.
we provide a general framework to study the topological stability of FSs and topologically nontrival edge-modes (or MFs) for fermionic systems with PHS, which can be used to predict new types of MFs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boundary-bulk correspondence of topological insulators/superconductors can be used to predict the existence of new types of Majorana fermions.
the bulk-edge correspondence is the fundamental principle to search for MFs, and the topological stabilities are the key ingredients to classify MFs.
we have established a general and rigorous relation between FS topology and TIs/TSCs, which is a key ingredient to understand and classify the new MF types.
